To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the incidence of fatal myocardial infarctions was increased for 4 years among residents who were exposed to the 2011 tsunami in Japan.

the incidence of fatal myocardial infarctions (MIs) increased in areas affected by the 2011 Great East Japan earthquake and tsunami and that the incidence was correlated with the percentage area inundated by the tsunami.

the incidence of fatal myocardial infarctions was increased in the 3 years following the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and tsunami, particularly in municipalities where the inundated area exceeded 10% of the residential area.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the long-term health effects of the 3/11 earthquake and tsunami.
the impact of the tsunami on the incidence and mortality of cardiovascular diseases in Miyagi Prefecture.
the long-term effects on the incidence of myocardial infarctions (MI).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the devastating tsunami that occurred in 2011 was associated with a sustained increase in the incidence rate of fatal MI among survivors in the high-impacted area.
the devastating tsunami associated with the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake was associated with a sustained increase in the incidence rate of fatal myocardial infarctions among survivors.
the 2011 tsunami caused a long-term increase in the incidence rate of fatal myocardial infarctions among the disaster-affected population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 2011 earthquake and tsunami had a long-term impact on the incidence of nonfatal and fatal MI in the disaster areas of Japan.
the 2011 tsunami was associated with an increased incidence of fatal MI for 4 years after the disaster.
the 2011 tsunami caused the increase in the incidence rate of fatal MI among the disaster survivors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tsunami was associated with an increase in the incidence rate of fatal MI in the disaster area.
the tsunami disaster had a sustained effect on fatal MI incidence, and the effect was associated with the magnitude of the disaster.
the tsunami was associated with the increase of fatal MI incidence among disaster survivors.
